AL.name: Butler County Schools
AL.quote: The Board shall allow reasonable corporal punishment only after other means of discipline have failed to produce desirable results. If corporal punishment is required, it shall be administered only by a certified employee in the presence of a school administrator who has been informed beforehand of the reasons for the punishment. At no time shall corporal punishment be administered in the presence of another student. Parents who object to corporal punishment as a method of discipline shall advise the school administrator in writing of the objection; however, the school administrator has the authority to determine appropriate discipline
AL.policy_code: 2026-2027 Code of Conduct, section "Corporal Punishment" (p. 14, under Formal Disciplinary Actions and Procedures)
AL.notes: Opt-out only, and non-binding: parents who object must advise the administrator in writing, but the text says the administrator retains authority to determine discipline, and the signature page reads "I DO___ or DO NOT ___ prefer that corporal punishment (paddling) be used ... However, I acknowledge the right of the school system's authority to use any and all disciplinary measures ... including paddling." Administered by a certified employee with a Board-issued paddle, no more than three licks, in the presence of a school administrator (or principal's designee), after an attempted phone call to the parent, recorded in PowerSchool, with a written explanation and witness name given to parents afterward. No disability exemption is stated. Document is the district's "2026-2027 Code of Conduct" PDF linked from https://www.butlerco.k12.al.us/for-parents/bcss-handbook-policies (BCSS Handbook & Policies page), which also lists "Board Policy/Student Handbook & Code of Conduct Revisions" dated July 17, 2025 and October 16, 2025. The Code of Conduct cites Alabama Code 16-28A-1 and Ingraham v. Wright. Corporal punishment is listed as a first-offense option for Class II (grades 6-12) and Class III offenses. No separate board policy manual (AASB-style) was found on the district site; the Code of Conduct is board-adopted and is the operative text.

AL.name: Calhoun County School District
AL.quote: In accordance with Alabama law, the Board of Education permits the use of corporal punishment. Should corporal punishment be needed, it must be administered in accordance with the following: The student has been notified of the offense for which he/she is to receive corporal punishment and the student has been given an opportunity to explain his/her actions. The punishment shall be administered by the school principal or his/her designee(s) (certificated personnel only) and witnessed by a certified school employee. The punishment shall be administered out of the view or presence of any other students. The punishment shall consist of no more than three swats on the buttocks with a smooth surface paddle free of holes and/or cracks.
AL.notes: Board policy 6.16 contains no parental consent or opt-out provision. Administered by the principal or certificated designee, witnessed by a certified employee, out of view of other students, maximum three swats with a smooth paddle; no disability exemption stated. The 2026-2027 Student Code of Conduct discipline tables list 'Corporal Punishment and Parental Notification-as a last resort after other disciplinary tactics have failed and/or determined on a case by-case basis' (notification, not consent). Board Policy Manual on Simbli (S=36031575), linked from https://www.calhouncountyschools.com/our-district/policies-reports. Policy 6.16 'Corporal Punishment', status ADOPTED, original adopted 06/06/2023, last reviewed 06/06/2023, reference ALA. CODE §16-28A-2. The 2026-2027 Student Code of Conduct PDF (https://resources.finalsite.net/images/v1782915796/calhounk12alus/wufdubppvm8ain3uk87i/StudentCodeofConduct.pdf) repeats the policy text verbatim under 'Corporal Punishment-' in its definitions of disciplinary actions and, under STUDENT DUE PROCESS, provides 'Informal Due Process - Corporal Punishment and Short-Term Suspension (9 days or less)' (oral or written notice of the charge, explanation of the evidence, opportunity to present the student's version). The CCBOE Student Handbook PDF (https://resources.finalsite.net/images/v1782915853/calhounk12alus/ngt0vriwbhw6mnll9nvt/CCBOE_Student_Handbook.pdf) contains no corporal punishment text. District office: 4400 McClellan Blvd, Anniston, AL 36206. calhoun.k12.al.us redirects to calhouncountyschools.com. Stable entry point: https://simbli.eboardsolutions.com/Policy/PolicyListing.aspx?S=36031575 then chapter 6 > 6.16.

AL.name: Coffee County Schools
AL.quote: The Board allows reasonable corporal punishment of students under the following terms and conditions. Corporal punishment will be administered only as a disciplinary measure, with due regard for the age and physical condition of the student, and without excessive force. Administered by the principal, assistant principal, or designee in the presence of another certified employee, not in the presence of another student; no disability exemption stated in the policy. Corporal punishment for a student documented as having a disability, in which the behavior was not a manifestation of the student's disability, will follow the same procedures as a non-disabled student.

AL.name: Dale County Board of Education (Dale County Schools)

AL.name: DeKalb County Board of Education (DeKalb County Schools)
AL.quote: 6.14.1 Corporal Punishment - Corporal punishment shall always be administered with a consideration for the age and physical maturity of the student. Corporal punishment must always be a deliberate, well thought out action on the part of school administrators and should be administered appropriately to effectively alter student behaviors that are unacceptable in a school environment. Should corporal punishment be needed, it must be administered according to the following: a. A student must be notified of the offense for which he/she is to receive corporal punishment and the student must be given an opportunity to explain his/her actions. b. The punishment must be administered by a school administrator and witnessed by a certified school employee. c. The punishment must be administered out of view of any other students. d. The punishment shall consist of a moderate use of physical force or physical contact by an administrator as may be necessary to maintain discipline or to enforce school rules. e. A written record of the punishment shall be made, in which the violated offense resulting in the punishment is listed along with the administered punishment, the name of the witness(es), and the name of the administrator giving the discipline. The administrator shall maintain a copy of the record and a copy shall be given to the student's parent/guardian.
AL.notes: No parental consent or opt-out; the 2026-2027 Student Handbook and Code of Conduct sec. 5.3.3 states verbatim: 'State law does not forbid corporal punishment. The DeKalb County Board of Education does not recognize a "no paddle" list. Schools must follow IEP/504 plan or make provisions for medical reasons.' Administered by a school administrator, witnessed by a certified employee, out of view of other students, written record with copy to parent. Policy manual is 'Policies and Procedures Handbook', 228 pages, cover reads 'Effective 8/1/2026' (page footers carry 'DRAFT 5/21/15' watermark). Linked from https://www.dekalbk12.org/handbooks. Companion source: 2026-2027 Student Handbook and Code of Conduct, https://files.smartsites.parentsquare.com/12948/26-27_student_handbook_final_1.pdf, sec. 5.3.3 (p. 2295 of text extraction) and the Type I / Type II offense sanction lists ('Corporal Punishment - (Witness and Due Process Required) - DeKalb County Board of Education Policy must be followed').

AL.name: Pike County Schools
AL.quote: The Pike County Board of Education prohibits the use of corporal punishment. No person employed by or engaged in the Pike County Schools shall administer corporal punishment upon a pupil.
AL.notes: Not applicable; the policy prohibits corporal punishment outright. It substitutes a one-day suspension with a required parent conference on return for Code of Conduct violations. Policy 5.30.1 CORPORAL PUNISHMENT, Status ADOPTED, Original Adopted Date 06/01/2005, Last Revised Date 06/17/2024, Last Reviewed Date 06/17/2024, on the district's Simbli manual (linked from https://www.pikecountyschools.com/ as the board policy listing, S=36031835). CONFLICT WITH CRDC: the ban was revised 06/17/2024, after the 2023-24 school year in which CRDC records 252 students receiving corporal punishment, so the 2023-24 figure likely reflects the pre-June-2024 policy. Simbli does not expose the prior revision text publicly; board minutes from June 2024 were not located (no search budget). Recommend a [conflict] issue only if a later data year still shows paddling.

GA.name: Laurens County Schools
GA.quote: Any principal or other designated school administrator employed by the Board of Education, in order to maintain proper control and discipline over pupils under his or her care and supervision, may, in the exercise of sound discretion, administer corporal punishment to any pupil or pupils under his or her care and supervision.
GA.notes: Opt-out: "Corporal punishment shall not be administered to a child whose parents or legal guardian have filed with the principal of the school a statement expressly objecting to the use of corporal punishment or a statement from a medical doctor licensed in Georgia stating that corporal punishment is detrimental to the child's mental or emotional stability." Only a principal or designated administrator may administer it, never a teacher or parent; it must be witnessed by another certified employee informed beforehand in the pupil's presence; a written explanation and the witness's name are provided to parents on request; it may not be excessive and generally not a first-line punishment. No IEP/504 exemption beyond the doctor's-statement route. Simbli/eBoard (GSBA) board policy manual, site S=4101, reached from https://www.lcboe.net/338421_2 (Board of Education page, link 'eBoard - Laurens County' -> https://simbli.eboardsolutions.com/Index.aspx?S=4101). Policy JDA status ADOPTED, Original Adopted Date 02/14/2008, Last Reviewed Date 08/13/2020. References O.C.G.A. 20-2-730 through 20-2-732. Simbli listing is JavaScript-rendered; the ViewPolicy link was obtained by filtering the listing to section J in a browser.

MS.name: Chickasaw County School District
MS.quote: Reasonable corporal punishment of a non-disabled student is permitted as a disciplinary measure in order to preserve an effective educational environment which is free from disruption and is conducive to furthering the educational mission of the board.
MS.notes: No parental consent or opt-out provision appears in policy JDB. Disability exemption: "School personnel is prohibited from using corporal punishment on any student with a disability. A student with a disability is any student who has an IEP or Section 504 plan." It may be administered by the principal, assistant principal, or a teacher, in the presence of another school employee, only after less stringent measures have failed unless the conduct is extreme; must be reasonable and moderate. MSBA policy service: the district's Board of Trustees page https://www.chickasaw.k12.ms.us/page/board-of-trustees/ links 'Board Policies Public View' -> https://chickasaw.msbapolicy.org/ which redirects to Simbli site S=36031690. Policy JDB status ADOPTED, Original Adopted Date 07/20/2012, Last Revised Date 06/08/2026, Last Reviewed Date 06/08/2026. Cites Miss. Code 37-11-57 and 11-46-9, Ingraham v. Wright; cross-references AAA and JD. District office is in Houston, MS.

MS.name: Scott County School District

MS.name: South Panola School District
MS.quote: The South Panola School District policy allows corporal punishment under certain conditions. Contact your school for an opt-out form for you to sign if you choose not to have your child paddled.
MS.policy_code: Batesville Middle School 2026-2027 Student Handbook, "Discipline" section, "CORPORAL PUNISHMENT (CP)" (p. 11); Appendix E: Corporal Punishment (p. 42)
MS.notes: The handbook text frames it as opt-out ("Contact your school for an opt-out form ... if you choose not to have your child paddled"). Appendix E is a signed form with two boxes: "South Panola School District Administration has my permission to use corporal punishment as a means to correct behavior. Prior to issuing corporal punishment, a phone call will be made to the parent/guardian." and "South Panola School District does NOT have my permission to use corporal punishment as a means to correct behavior." No witness, administrator, or disability provisions are stated in the handbook; the underlying board policy could not be read (see notes). The district's board policy manual is on MSBA/Simbli (southpanola.msbapolicy.org -> https://simbli.eboardsolutions.com/Index.aspx?S=36031786), but the policy listing redirects to https://simbli.eboardsolutions.com/Login.aspx?S=36031786 and is not publicly readable, so the status rests on the school handbook, which states district policy. The handbook is the Batesville Middle School (grades 4-5) 2026-2027 Parent/Student Handbook, linked from https://www.spsd.k12.ms.us/o/bams/documents/ (also via short link https://aptg.co/hnYHRQ). It lists corporal punishment as a consequence for 2nd-offense minor bus infractions, 2nd-offense electronic device use, tardies, and vandalism on the disciplinary referral form. Possible internal tension: the discipline section describes an opt-out, while the Appendix E form is worded as permission/no permission; recorded here as allows (opt-out) per the policy sentence. Other school handbooks (SPHS, BJHS, BIS, Pope, BAES) were not found in their document folders. District office is in Batesville, MS.

MS.name: West Jasper School District
MS.quote: CORPORAL PUNISHMENT Reasonable corporal punishment of a student is permitted as a disciplinary measure in order to preserve an effective educational environment which is free from disruption and is conducive to furthering the educational mission of the board. Parents or guardians are not allowed to administer corporal punishment on West Jasper School District grounds. Students who cannot be given corporal punishment may be suspended out of school for offenses which would merit corporal punishment.
MS.notes: No parental consent or opt-out provision; 'Students who cannot be given corporal punishment may be suspended out of school for offenses which would merit corporal punishment.' Administered by the teacher, principal or assistant principal (lead teachers may be authorized), 'not to exceed three licks per day', 'in the presence of a certified employee'; 'HB1182, corporal punishment is prohibited for students with a disability who has an IEP or Section 504 Plan. West Jasper School District will suspend any student with a disability who has an IEP or Section 504 Plan, rather than administer corporal punishment.' Handbook is 'West Jasper School District School Year 2026-27' (62 pages), linked from westjasper.org. The K-6 and 7-12 discipline step plans list 'One day ISD or Corporal Punishment' (steps 1-3), the tardy policy lists 'Corporal punishment or 1 day of ISD' at the 4th unexcused tardy, and bus offenses list corporal punishment as an option for the first three minor/intermediate offenses. The district's board policy manual link (https://wjasper.msbapolicy.org/) redirects to Simbli (https://simbli.eboardsolutions.com/Index.aspx?S=36031853), whose policy listing requires JavaScript and returned no policy text to curl or WebFetch; no Wayback capture found. The MSBA policy code (likely JDA) could not be confirmed. CRDC name 'WEST JASPER CONSOLIDATED SCHOOLS'; NCES and district style it 'West Jasper School District'.

TX.name: Big Spring Independent School District
TX.quote: Corporal punishment may be used as a discipline management technique in accordance with this policy and the Student Code of Conduct. Corporal punishment shall not be administered to a student whose parent has submitted to the principal a signed statement for the current school year prohibiting the use of corporal punishment with his or her child. The parent may reinstate permission to use corporal punishment at any time during the school year by submitting a signed statement to the principal.
TX.notes: Opt-out only: not administered to a student whose parent has submitted to the principal a signed statement for the current school year prohibiting it; the parent may reinstate permission at any time by signed statement. Limited to spanking or paddling, administered only by the principal or designee (a female principal or designee when the student is female), with one other District professional employee present, out of view of other students; the disciplinary record must include the administrator, witness, date and time. No disability exemption in FO(LOCAL); FO(LEGAL) carries the Education Code 37.0011 opt-out text. TASB Policy Online, Big Spring ISD Board Policy Manual key=685 (linked from https://www.bsisd.esc18.net/about-bsisd/board-of-trustees as 'Board Policy Manual'). FO(LOCAL)-X, UPDATE 126, DATE ISSUED: 10/17/2025. Guidelines text: 'Corporal punishment shall be limited to spanking or paddling the student and shall be administered in accordance with the following guidelines: The student shall be told the reason corporal punishment is being administered. Corporal punishment shall be administered only by the principal or designee, and, when the student is female, only by a female principal or designee. The instrument to be used in administering corporal punishment shall be approved by the principal. Corporal punishment shall be administered in the presence of one other District professional employee and in a designated place out of view of other students.' The 2026-2027 BSISD Student Code of Conduct (https://resources.finalsite.net/images/v1786994858/bsisdesc18net/tcg7xqznfcxufropnwcz/2026-2027BSISDStudentCodeofConduct.pdf, p.12 'Discipline Management Techniques') lists: 'Corporal punishment, unless the student’s parent or guardian has provided a signed statement prohibiting its use.' and under Prohibited Aversive Techniques: 'Using techniques designed or likely to cause physical pain, other than corporal punishment as permitted by district policy. [See policy FO(LOCAL).]' District office: 708 East 11th Place, Big Spring, TX 79720. Board agendas/minutes: https://meetings.boardbook.org/Public/Organization/723.

TX.quote: Corporal punishment may be used as a discipline management technique in accordance with this policy and the Student Code of Conduct. Corporal punishment shall not be administered to a student whose parent has submitted to the principal a signed statement for the current school year prohibiting the use of corporal punishment with his or her child. The parent may reinstate permission to use corporal punishment at any time during the school year by submitting a signed statement to the principal.
TX.notes: Opt-out only: not administered to a student whose parent has submitted to the principal a signed statement for the current school year prohibiting it; the parent may reinstate permission at any time by signed statement. Limited to spanking or paddling, administered only by the principal or designee, with one other District professional employee present, in a designated place out of view of other students; the disciplinary record must include the administrator, witness, date and time. No disability exemption in FO(LOCAL); FO(LEGAL) carries the Education Code 37.0011 opt-out text. TASB Policy Online, Livingston ISD Board Policy Manual key=1001 (linked from https://www.livingstonisd.com/135616_2, the School Board page, as 'Board Policy Manual' https://pol.tasb.org/PolicyOnline?key=1001). FO(LOCAL)-C1, UPDATE 126, DATE ISSUED: 10/9/2025. Guidelines text: 'Corporal punishment shall be limited to spanking or paddling the student and shall be administered in accordance with the following guidelines: The student shall be told the reason corporal punishment is being administered. Corporal punishment shall be administered only by the principal or designee. The instrument to be used in administering corporal punishment shall be approved by the principal. Corporal punishment shall be administered in the presence of one other District professional employee and in a designated place out of view of other students.' Unlike Big Spring's FO(LOCAL), there is no same-sex-administrator clause. No student handbook or code of conduct PDF was located on livingstonisd.com this run. District office: 1412 South Houston Ave., Livingston, TX 77351. Board agendas/minutes: https://meetings.boardbook.org/Public/Organization/1664.

TX.name: Mount Pleasant ISD
TX.quote: Corporal punishment may be used as a discipline management technique in accordance with this policy and the Student Code of Conduct. Corporal punishment shall not be administered to a student whose parent has submitted to the principal a signed statement for the current school year prohibiting the use of corporal punishment with his or her child. The parent may reinstate permission to use corporal punishment at any time during the school year by submitting a signed statement to the principal.
TX.notes: Opt-out: a parent must submit a signed statement to the principal each school year prohibiting corporal punishment, and may reinstate permission at any time. Limited to spanking or paddling, administered only by the principal or designee with an instrument approved by the principal, in the presence of one other District professional employee and out of view of other students; the student is told the reason first; the disciplinary record must include the administrator, witness, date and time. FO(LOCAL) states no disability exemption. TASB Policy Online, Mount Pleasant ISD (district key 1133), FO(LOCAL)-C1, UPDATE 126, DATE ISSUED: 11/11/2025. The same page carries FO(LEGAL) quoting Education Code 37.0011 (parent's written, signed statement prohibits corporal punishment; must be provided each school year). Link to Policy Online found on the district homepage https://www.mpisd.net/ (http://pol.tasb.org/Home/Index/1133).
